trigger: POST /api/v1/result-sets/from-instruction-result had no bound at all on instruction_id/params
summary: from-instruction-result creation route dispatched fleet-wide with an unbounded instruction_id/params in one step, more directly exploitable than the re-eval smuggle path #4373 was filed for
classification_rationale: undisclosed sibling vulnerability of the same class the PR was fixing

trigger: instruction_store->is_open() ran before the new instruction_id/params bound checks on the creation route
summary: a malformed/oversized field arriving while the store is down got 503 instead of the intended 400, so a permanently-invalid request's retry_after_ms would never succeed
classification_rationale: contradicted the fix's own stated rationale ('regardless of backend availability')

trigger: std::format('{:0<256}', 'k{}') zero-fill collided k1/k10, k2/k20, k3/k30
summary: exact-boundary params test silently exercised 29 distinct keys instead of the intended 32, so it could not have caught a >= vs > off-by-one in the count guard
classification_rationale: test name/comment claimed exact-32-key coverage it did not provide

trigger: no test proved a genuine 256-byte instruction_id clears the length guard on the creation route
summary: missing coverage gap: only the 257-byte reject side was tested, not the 256-byte accept side, for instruction_id specifically
classification_rationale: a required regression case for a new guard's accept boundary

trigger: changelog bullet 3 claimed both routes gained the type-confusion guard
summary: the type-confusion guard had only landed on re-eval at that point, not from-instruction-result (independently caught by cpp-safety too)
classification_rationale: changelog asserted something the code diff did not do

summary: layering question about REST depending on an mcp_-prefixed shared header; confirmed established precedent (mcp_jsonrpc.hpp already used the same way), not a new coupling
classification_rationale: informational architecture note, no code change requested

trigger: changelog's 'Not fixed here, tracked separately' bullet implied all three disclosed gaps had tracking issues
summary: only #4406 had a real GitHub issue; the source_kind-allowlist and matcher/name/parent_id gaps were untracked, not tracked
classification_rationale: changelog asserted tracking evidence that did not exist

trigger: no docs/user-manual/server-admin.md Upgrade Notes entry for a breaking REST change
summary: the #2500/#2442 precedent requires an Upgrade Notes entry for a breaking-but-narrow REST change; missing at time of review
classification_rationale: required doc per the six-item list (item 2, changed operator-facing behavior)

trigger: params gated on is_object() everywhere; a string/array/number params skipped every bound check and the params-map-build loop
summary: a non-object params silently dispatched with an empty map (discarding caller intent) while persisting the wrong-shaped value verbatim and unbounded into source_payload, re-parsed on every future re-eval
classification_rationale: the bound-check gate itself created an unvalidated fallthrough this fix's own stated goal (bound the params field) did not cover

trigger: from-instruction-result's instruction_id extraction was the one of four near-identical copies lacking the is_string() guard
summary: a type-mismatched instruction_id threw an uncaught nlohmann::json::type_error, degrading to a bare HTTP 500; this is GitHub issue #4406, closed fully in the same fix (both fields, both creation routes)
classification_rationale: the diff's own updated OpenAPI 400-description text implied clean 400 coverage that this gap contradicted

trigger: server-admin.md's What-breaks table omitted the non-object-params row
summary: the same commit's changelog explicitly called the non-object-params rejection a behavior change but the upgrade-notes table did not list it (independently caught by consistency-auditor, docs-writer, and security-guardian)
classification_rationale: required doc, item 2, an operator-facing behavior change omitted from its own table

trigger: new comment cited '#2437-class' for the no-exception-handler fact
summary: '#2437-class' means the JSON-depth-guard convention everywhere else in this file; reusing it for an unrelated fact (missing exception handler) was a citation mislabel, not a wrong underlying claim
classification_rationale: citation convention drift, not a factual error

trigger: 2 of 4 new #4406 regression tests asserted status only, not message
summary: discipline gap versus this file's own established convention of asserting the specific error message, though regression detection was already sound since pre-fix behavior was a 500 not a differently-worded 400
classification_rationale: test-quality gap relative to house convention, not a false-green risk

trigger: MCP's create_result_set_from_instruction_result and reevaluate_result_set have the identical present-but-non-object params gap
summary: neither MCP tool rejects a non-object params; {"params": null} also diverges (REST now 400s, MCP silently treats as absent) - disclosed in the changelog, not fixed, since this PR is REST-only
classification_rationale: a sibling gap on a different transport, genuinely out of this PR's scope
waiver_rationale: MCP is a different transport/file not touched by this REST-only bound-checking PR; disclosed in the changelog fragment rather than silently left unstated; operator has not authorized filing a new tracking issue for it yet
